Thanks for the detailed report. PGRST303 means PostgREST rejected a JWT claim, and the `message` field says which one (for example, exp, iat, nbf or aud). Could you log it on the failing call and share it here?

```ts
const { error } = await supabase.rpc('is_admin')
if (error) console.error(error.code, error.message, new Date().toISOString())
```

The error code reference is here: https://supabase.com/docs/guides/api/rest/postgrest-error-codes#authentication-errors

This may be the same problem as #50124, which also reports PGRST303 right after a successful Auth sign-in on a hosted project. The exact message and the UTC time of a failing request will help narrow it down.
final_draft: Thanks for the report. If the error message is "JWT issued at future", this matches a known PostgREST bug where fresh tokens are rejected right after sign-in. It looks like the same problem as issue 50124, and the fix is in PostgREST 14.18 and later, while your project reports 14.5. A restart (Settings > General > Restart project) has cleared it temporarily for some projects. To get the fixed version, please contact Supabase support with your project reference and the UTC time of a failing request, and link this issue. Please don't post access tokens or keys here.

original_draft: Thanks for the detailed report. The error looks like the dashboard sends the partition and retention intervals as unquoted numbers, while pgmq.create_partitioned expects text, so the call fails to resolve. Basic and unlogged queues are not affected, so a workaround is to create the partitioned queue in the SQL editor with quoted intervals, for example select from pgmq.create_partitioned('my_queue', '10000', '100000');. For the project stuck in COMING_UP, that is specific to your account, so please contact Supabase support through the dashboard rather than this tracker. Also, if you can share your pgmq extension version from select extversion from pg_extension where extname = 'pgmq';, that would help.
